public_rationale: The NYT article Marcus cites, by Thompson and Myers on June 26, 2025, documents AI-generated fake photos and videos of candidates spreading in elections. It cites an independent panel that found AI used in over 80% of 2024 elections worldwide, with 215 documented instances and a harmful role in 69% of cases. It also reports that officials said an AI-enabled Russian operation tainted Romania's 2024 presidential first round, which a court annulled. An election law expert calls the headline overstated but agrees the cases are real. 'Starting to see misinformation on the world stage' fits this record.
limitations: How much AI changed election outcomes is disputed. This assessment covers presence, not decisive impact.
The NYT text was read through a syndicated copy and an excerpt.

conditions: citing NYT article 'A.I. Is Starting to Wear Down Democracy'

statement.excerpt: Item 5, from the NYT last week, in article called A.I. Is Starting to Wear Down Democracy: we are starting to see misinformation play out on the world stage:

from_speaker: A.I. Is Starting to Wear Down Democracy
our_interpretation: Plain reading: by mid-2025, AI-generated misinformation, such as deepfakes of candidates, was documented in elections and political events across several countries.
'Starting to' sets a low bar. Documented spread is enough; proof that AI decided an outcome is not required.
The period runs from the 2024 global election wave to the post date.
criteria.support_condition: Credible reporting or research from 2024 to mid-2025 documents AI-generated misinformation in elections or international political events in several countries.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible research finds no meaningful AI-generated misinformation in elections or international politics in this period.
